title: Book One · Chapter 117: The Wavy Pages
story:
The two exercise books lie open on a table at school. Their pages are no longer wet. The pages are wavy, not flat.

Mr Qiu and Mum have taken four books home. Miss Wu checked them yesterday. They are in the first crate. They are not with his flat, clean books. Miss Wu must still check these last two.

Leo gives Ronan the short yellow ruler. He borrowed it from Ronan. Ronan puts it in his pencil case. Then he looks at the books.

Ronan presses one page with his hand. It rises again when he lets go.

“It likes the air,” Leo says.

“It was never this big before.”

The book looks too full for its cover. Ronan puts his finger near the edge. He wants to pull two pages apart.

“Wait,” Miss Wu says. She sets her own books down. “Let me look.”

She lifts a corner slowly. The paper makes a small sound. She stops.

“These two still need time.”

“Mr Qiu needs his books.”

“He does. If you pull them now, the pages may tear. We need to wait.”

She puts a clean sheet under the open cover. Then she moves the table away from the window. Wind sometimes blows rain through the open part.

Ronan helps her move a chair. It is a safe, small job. He wishes it were a larger one.

At noon he walks to the green gate with Mum. Mr Qiu is in Mrs Lan's front room. The two wooden crates stand against the wall. A large number is on each one.

“Still drying,” Ronan tells him.

“Thank you for looking.”

“We can make them flat again.”

Mr Qiu looks at the rain outside.

“Can you?”

Ronan thinks about the page under his hand.

“I don't know yet.”

Mr Qiu nods. He lifts a pencil box from the second crate. The pencils are dry. Their bright ends stand in a neat row.

“These are ready,” he says. “That is something.”

Mrs Lan comes in with a cup. She stops at the open crate.

“I need my front room tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr Qiu puts the pencil box down.

“Of course.”

“My sister is coming. She brings a very large bag.”

Mum laughs, but Mr Qiu does not. He looks at the crates.

“We can put them by our door,” Ronan says.

“We cannot,” Mum says. “There is no dry space there.”

Ronan looks through the doorway. Their small room is at the back of the yard. His books are on the low shelf. Mum's work bag is beside the table. Dad's shoes are under his chair.

He looks for another dry corner. He cannot find room for two big crates.

“Tomorrow morning,” Mrs Lan says, “we can talk about the space by the gate. Only talk, first.”

Mr Qiu picks up his cup with both hands.

“I would like that.”

Later Ronan finds a sheet in his school bag. He has drawn Mr Qiu's closed stall on it. The roof is dark with rain. There are words under the picture too. He wrote a line about Mr Qiu. Mr Qiu needs help, he thought.

He folds the paper before Mum can read it.

“Is that for Mr Qiu?” she asks.

“It may be. I have to ask him.”

“Then keep it in your bag for now.”

Ronan puts it between two dry books. Across the yard, Mr Qiu closes the first crate. He lowers the lid slowly. Then he checks the lid. It is shut.

Ronan reads the first line again. Then he puts his bag down. The line says: Mr Qiu has lost his books. Mr Qiu asked him to help dry paper. Mr Qiu did not ask Ronan to call everyone for help. Ronan puts one finger over the line. The picture looks different without it. The old man is still there, under the roof, with his hand on a book.

---

重点表达：wavy＝起伏不平的；pull apart＝拉开；for now＝暂时。

情节提示：exercise book＝练习本；crate＝装货的大木箱；pencil case＝铅笔盒。

理解：1. Miss Wu 为什么不让 Ronan 拉开书页？2. Mrs Lan 明天需要使用什么空间？
